doc.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: Making a living: studio and odd work
title: Hollywood studio work in the late 1960s and 70s
summary: Studio work just happened to him, forcing him to woodshed and sight-read; he still receives checks for old shows.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: But I think Tatum really meant that when he said it. But I’ve done a lot of different kinds of work and then I ended up doing studio work in L.A. in Hollywood from about late ‘60s to the late ‘70s, about a ten year period. And I didn’t set out to do that. I don’t think many guys in the studios, men or women, set out to become studio players. I mean that’s not like a lifelong dream as a kid, it just happens. If you’re in a particular area like Los Angeles or New York where there’s a lot of that work and you happen to get a few of the calls, and if you’re halfway good at it, word of mouth and referrals, you begin to get a few more calls. So I ended up doing a lot of that. And it was a great experience really, because among other things I had to really go back and woodshed the instrument. Some of the stuff you’re called upon to do in a motion picture score for instance, really requires some pretty serious playing as far as sight reading and performance skills. And it forced me to kind of, again to re-evaluate my own playing. A lot of it was just craft, it wasn’t high art you know, playing on a T.V. show score. But within that context you can still get a lot out of it.
Do you ever hear anything on the television reruns or whatever, and say hey, I played on that?

You know I hardly watch television, I’m sure there are, I still get checks for stuff, a show that’s playing in Finland that I did in 1967 or something. But I don’t watch enough T.V. to know. But I know, yeah, that some of them are still playing. I did a Rice-a-Roni commercial that was on for about twenty years.
